question: Does a MinGW-w64 C++11 static library, linked into a MinGW-w64 Win32 executable, run on Windows 2000 SP4?
result: Open, kept open on purpose: the question names Windows 2000 SP4 and the system tested has NO service pack (RTM, build 2195), so SP4 is still untested; the lead decides the status. TRIAL (2026-11-12): Windows 2000 Professional build 2195, no service pack, English (US), in a VirtualBox 7.2.22 VM (1 vCPU, 168 MB RAM, Guest Additions 6.1.18) on the Windows 11 host; records validation/platforms/windows-2000-x86.json and validation/verdicts/windows-2000-x86-legacy.json (ok_restricted), evidence in validation/evidence/first-trial/windows-2000-x86/, tooling in adr/0003-win2000-vm-unicode-launcher.md. WHAT RAN AND WORKED: the i686 Legacy UI executable (694,005 bytes: the MinGW-w64 GCC 13 C++11 static library libloomora.a linked into a Win32 exe with libstdc++ and libgcc static, ADR 0002 shim for GetThreadId) loads and runs. All 112 imports of the executable are exported by the real kernel32.dll 5.0.2191.1, user32.dll 5.0.2180.1, gdi32.dll 5.0.2180.1 and msvcrt.dll 6.1.8637.0 of that system (export tables read; 0 missing), and all 117 functions of the x86 allowlist tools/win2000_imports.json are exported (0 missing); the 12 entries marked verify (TryEnterCriticalSection, the msvcrt.dll start-up internals) are now verified-on-vm for x86 (RTM export tables, not SP4's). The window shows the end-of-life banner, 'Bonjour Coucou', and 'Bonjour Marie' when typed with the virtual keyboard (screenshots); 20 of 20 probe runs: exit 0, display_ms 3 to 13, peak_rss_kb 1084 (checked plausible with memtest and WMI, not a defect), no process left; 15 of 15 reference vectors and 25 of 25 extra hard texts (emoji, CJK, right-to-left, controls, quotes, backslashes, %PATH%, 1,500 characters) round-trip unchanged; exits by itself after 2 s and with Alt+F4. Skipped features on this system: dpi-awareness (user32 does not export SetProcessDPIAware) and dark-mode (no AppsUseLightTheme); GetNativeSystemInfo is absent and the fallback GetSystemInfo is taken; dwmapi.dll is absent. FINDING (part of the spike is refuted for the backend test program): loomora_selftest cross-built with cmake/toolchains/mingw-w64-win2000-i686.cmake does NOT load on Windows 2000: it imports KERNEL32!GetThreadId (removed by the ADR 0002 shim) and, with or without the shim, four Vista-only functions (InitializeConditionVariable, SleepConditionVariableCS, WakeConditionVariable, WakeAllConditionVariable) from libgcc.a(gthr-win32-cond.o), pulled in by its use of <iostream> (libstdc++ ios_init); the loader refuses it (exit status 128, no output), exactly like a control program that imports InitializeConditionVariable, while a control program with Windows 2000 imports runs. The Legacy UI, which links the same libloomora.a but no iostream, is not affected. To decide (not done here): extend the shim of ADR 0002 to those functions, or keep iostream out of selftest.cpp, or fallback (2) of R6 (another MinGW-w64/GCC version or thread model). STILL UNVERIFIED: Windows 2000 SP4 (and the SP4 msvcrt.dll, which is a later build than this RTM one); real hardware instead of VirtualBox; other languages, editions and machines; a person typing, IME, clipboard, a high contrast scheme, DPI above 96; the behaviour of a C++ exception thrown in the static runtime (none was thrown); the 1,000-character EDIT limit by keyboard on this system; Windows 2000 x64 does not exist (N/A); XP and later (S9) and the x64 executable on XP x64 / Server 2003 x64 are not covered.

question: Does modern Clang + osxcross + the 10.6 SDK run on 10.6; does Xcode 5.1.1 build and deploy to iOS 5?
Does NDK r16b + the scripted APK build run on an Android 2.3 emulator (all four ABIs)?
Does the manylinux2010 build need only glibc <= 2.12 and run on a 2010-era distribution?
Does the JavaScript build run on IE 9 / Firefox 8 / Chrome 15 / Safari 5.1 / Opera 11.5; modern Emscripten or fastcomp 1.39.20?
Does the backend compile with strict C++11 under GCC and Clang and export only C symbols, with every exception caught at the C boundary?
result: Confirmed on Linux (WSL Ubuntu 24.04, libstdc++): tools/check_std.py passes with g++ 13.3.0 and clang++ 23.1.5. Checked for each: all 6 core/src/*.cpp compile with -std=c++11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror; loomora.h compiles as C89 (-std=c89 -pedantic-errors, gcc 13.3.0 / clang 23.1.5) and as C++98; a shared library built with -fvisibility=hidden exports exactly the 6 loomora_* C functions (nm -D --defined-only), with the C++ runtime linked dynamically and statically (-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc); core/tests/boundary_check.cpp makes every allocation of every loomora_* call fail in turn (28 failures injected with GCC, 30 with Clang) and no exception escapes. Finding: -fvisibility=hidden alone is NOT enough, libstdc++ marks namespace std as default visibility and std template instantiations leaked into the exports (4 with g++, 16 with clang++); fixed with a link-time export list (core/loomora.map, core/loomora.exp for macOS) that CMake and check_std.py apply to the shared library. Not checked: strict C++11 with clang on Windows (clang 23.1.1 uses the MSVC STL, which needs C++14: the checker reports it as skipped; only the C89/C++98 header checks ran there), libc++, MSVC, Windows DLL exports (__declspec macros untested), macOS exports (loomora.exp untested), and the old compilers of the oldest platforms (S1-S4).
